newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM dissolves parliament, prepares for polls.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM dissolves parliament, prepares for polls.

text.p: Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto dissolved Japan's parliament on Friday, a move to be followed by a special cabinet session in the afternoon to formally set a date for general elections.
Elections for the 500-seat Lower House must be held within 40 days of a dissolution, but politicians and media have for weeks said the polls will be on October 20, eight months earlier than mandated.

Hashimoto's decision to dissolve the Lower House for an election ends weeks of wrangling between his Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) and its two smaller coalition partners over the timing of the polls.

The dispute over an election date between the LDP, which has a well-oiled electoral machine ready for early polls, and the fractious, election-shy Social Democratic Party and New Party Sakigake, has overshadowed policy debate in what many analysts predict will be an issue-free contest.
Hashimoto is expected to pin his hopes for a second term on an improving economy and his handling of a bitter dispute with the southern prefecture of Okinawa over U.S. military bases there.

The opposition Shinshinto (New Frontier Party) plans to attack the government for imposing an unpopular sales tax rise scheduled for next April and offer its own plan for a drastic overhaul of the tax system and to cut bureaucratic red tape.
